newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UOB sees growth in fee-based income.
newsitem.headline: UOB sees growth in fee-based income.

text.p: Singapore's United Overseas Bank Ltd said on Thursday it expected part of its future growth to come from fee-based operations such as managing initial public share offerings (IPOs).
UOB chairman and chief executive officer Wee Cho Yaw told reporters at the bank's 1996 financial results briefing that the banking industry was changing.

"Today in banking we have to be, in my view, not only in lending. Lending is risky and also the margins are very low. We should therefore look more into fee-based and more advisory type of roles," he said.
"I think that is where our growth will be focused."
Wee said the bank had to control operational costs if it wanted to meet the declared target of double-digit net profit growth in 1997.
"We need to reduce costs as much as possible and be more efficient," he said.
